column7: DeleteSecret/RestoreSecret's shared emitDependencyLifecycleEvents helper (internal/core/secret_dependencies.go) correctly treated a returned error from its own best-effort ListSecretDependenciesForProject call as non-fatal (its own doc comment says so), but had no protection against a PANIC from that same call -- a panic propagated straight through DeleteSecret/RestoreSecret (which had already committed the delete/restore several lines earlier) and out to the real Recovery middleware, producing an honest-looking 500 that actually masked an already-successful delete/restore (oracle (a): SecretNode state changed despite a reported error). Found live by an unattended final-checks fuzz burst. Fixed by recovering from a panic in emitDependencyLifecycleEvents the same way it already handled a returned error -- log and return, never surface to the caller. Proving test is the fuzz harness itself -- corpus entry 059212c4cda84764 is the permanent regression; see docs/findings/2026-09-22-FINDING-secret-delete-restore-dependency-emission-panic-masks-success.md
